name: MI-12
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 21 points, anchoring the race firmly on Tlaib's side
Tlaib holds a roughly 2,000-to-1 cash advantage over James Hooper, with no outside spending against her
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 98 percent
No general-election polling; a Green candidate and two independents also appear on the ballot
model.rationale: The district's 21-point Democratic lean, Tlaib's incumbency, and a nearly 2,000-to-1 fundraising gap leave the Republican without a visible path, and markets price the race near 98 percent Democratic. Every available signal points to a comfortable incumbent win in the mid-twenties or better.
model.watch: Only an unforeseen scandal or an unusually strong minor-party showing could narrow the margin, and neither would plausibly put the seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Rashida Tlaib enters the general election as a heavy favorite in this Detroit-area district, which leans Democratic by about 21 points. She has raised roughly $2.8 million and holds $3.4 million on hand, while Republican James Hooper has reported about $1,450 in receipts and under $8,000 in cash. No outside groups are spending against her, and prediction markets put her chances near 98 percent.

The ballot also includes a Green candidate and two independents, who could take small shares of the vote without changing the outcome. No public general-election polls are available, so the forecast rests on the district's partisan makeup, the lopsided money race, and the incumbent's established name recognition. Every available signal points the same direction: a comfortable Democratic win with a margin in the mid-twenties or better.
